q-107239.name: Question 1
q-107239.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14230697/assets/b892210357f67b41acf4e300f6ec4bc9e78a7c78ceda3c169105c33f02db7f8e.png)

What is the name of the polyhedron shown above?
q-107239.worked_solution:
The polyhedron is a **pentagonal prism** since it has two identical pentagonal faces connected by equal parallel line segments.

Also, notice that:

- The solid is not a pyramid since a pyramid must have triangular faces (except, possibly, for the base) that meet at a single point.

- The solid is not a rectangular prism since not all of its faces are rectangles.

q-93196.name: Question 5
q-93196.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14230697/assets/90bdf56a0c09a2db4fae7b19d3625360c4fc148b8807cc3e8a8ba35d1bdf78bb.png)

What is the name of the polyhedron shown above?
q-93196.worked_solution:
The solid is a **heptagonal pyramid** since it is a pyramid whose base is a heptagon.

Also, notice that:

- The solid is not a heptagonal prism since it has only one heptagonal face.

- The solid is not a hexagonal pyramid since it has no hexagonal face.

- The solid is not a rectangular prism since not all of its faces are rectangles. Due to the same reasons, the solid is not a cube.

q-107175.name: Question 7
q-107175.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14230697/assets/9a918919ef71c8e29b51d008fb5aa2720dbecbecc14830789b1f55fb259d47a5.png)

What is the name of the solid shown above?
q-107175.worked_solution:
The solid is an **oblique cylinder**. 

Notice the following:

- The solid has two parallel circular bases. So, it's a cylinder.

- The axis that passes through the centers of the circles is not perpendicular to the bases. So, it's oblique, not right.

What is the name of the solid shown above?
q-117677.worked_solution:
The solid is an **oblique cone**.

- The axis that passes through the center of the circle and the vertex is not perpendicular to the base. So, it's oblique, not right.
